newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland has no objection to BIG merger.
newsitem.headline: Poland has no objection to BIG merger.

text.p: The Polish anti-monopoly office has no objection to the planned merger between Bank Inicjatyw Gospodarczych SA (BIG) and Bank Gdanski SA, BIG said in a statement on Thursday.
"The Office for Competition and Consumer Protection voices no objection to the merger based on transferring all the property of Bank Gdanski...to (BIG)...in exchange for shares," the statement said.

To conclude the merger, which BIG wants to complete by the end of September and save 80 million to 100 million zlotys annually starting in 1999, an exchange of 11 BIG shares for each of Gdanski's would take place.

A BIG share issue of between 60 and 75 million shares received Securities Commission (KPW) approval on Thursday, up to 55 million shares of which can go toward GDRs which could be exchanged for Gdanski GDRs.
Gdanski has 19.5 percent of its shares in GDRs.
The planned merger still needs approval from the National Bank of Poland, the central bank.
BIG plans another share issue of 215,732,000 for an exchange for Gdanski shares and shareholders of the two banks are due to vote on the merger in late June.

The new entity, BIG Bank GDANSKI, would be the seventh largest Polish bank according to total assets, amounting to 7.9 billion zlotys, and fifth in terms of own funds, at 866 million zlotys. -- Warsaw Newsroom +48 22 653 9700
